entries.title: Spectrum Adaptation of AI-Native Autoencoder Communications with Transfer Learning
entries.abstract: End-to-end physical-layer learning replaces separate modulation, coding, and detection operations with an autoencoder (AE) that consists of a jointly trained encoder-decoder pair at the transmitter and the receiver. This paper studies AI-native communications with AEs and quantifies the sensitivity to training-test mismatch in channel models. Models trained only on an AWGN channel achieve low bit error rates (BERs) under matched conditions but degrade severely on Rayleigh fading with practical front-end impairments. To reduce the time and energy required to adapt to new channel conditions, we propose a low-latency transfer-learning procedure that starts from an AWGN-pretrained system and fine-tunes only a small subset of transmitter and receiver layers while freezing the remainder. We further formulate layer selection as a budget-constrained optimization problem that identifies the most informative parameters to update during adaptation. This preserves the learned signal geometry and the deep decision structure while adapting lightweight front ends to fading- and impairment-induced mixing. For AE communications, we show that partial updates remove the mismatch-induced error floor and approach the BER of fully retrained models. We provide a layer-wise study and quantify resource-performance trade-offs, showing that modest adaptation substantially reduces BER while cutting training time, multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations, energy consumption, and the fraction of updated parameters for resource-efficient implementation.

entries.title: Sliding-Window Detection of Hidden Regimes under Stochastic Switching
entries.abstract: A sliding-window average is a simple estimator of the current state of a hidden regime-switching process, such as a hidden Markov model. A longer window averages out more noise but is more likely to contain a switch, and the question is what such a switch costs. We analyse the decoder that assigns the average of the last m observations to the nearest regime mean. For two regimes with conditionally independent, stochastically ordered observations, a switch inside the window, averaged uniformly over its positions and directions, causes an error with probability exactly 1/2. Consequently, for every stationary switching law, the error is at most P(m)+s(m-1)/2, where P(m) is the stationary-weighted single-regime error and s the switch rate. Under Markov switching, time reversal shows that a window whose oldest and current regimes differ is misclassified with probability exactly 1/2, however many switches it contains, and the bound is attained up to a factor p_(min)^(m-1). For Gaussian noise with common variance, minimizing the bound gives an explicit window length which, in units of σ²/Δ², depends only on the expected number of switches in that time. As switching probabilities vanish proportionally, the optimal error is slog(1/s)/(2I)(1+o(1)), with I the single-regime Chernoff exponent. In the Gaussian case this is twice the Bayes error. For symmetric switching, exponentially weighted moving averages reduce this factor to at most 2log2≈1.39, and two-block weights adapted to the switch rate attain the Bayes rate. For three or more regimes, long-window switch costs are set by the geometry of the regime means. For Markov-modulated random walks with ±1 steps on a reflecting lattice, a position-aware decoder learns as fast as without walls under holding boundaries, while steps at bouncing boundaries carry none.
entries.comment: 29 pages, 8 figures. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24532266

entries.title: On the Distance Properties of Huffman Sequences
entries.abstract: In this letter, we study pairwise distances between sequences with a common aperiodic autocorrelation function. First, we show that pairwise distances are determined by a ternary signed pattern encoding the relative zero flips between spectral factors. Then, for Huffman sequences, we prove that Dihedral symmetries of the zeros preserve pairwise distances, and we further derive lower bounds on the minimum distance. The results in this letter offer a starting point for designing codes with a fixed autocorrelation. These codes are relevant in integrated sensing and communication.
entries.comment: This work has been accepted to IEEE Signal Processing Letters

entries.title: Device-Referred Channel Sounding With Commodity Wi-Fi Receivers: Error Budget and Body-Worn Measurements at 5 and 6 GHz
entries.abstract: A wireless product experiences the channel through its own antennas and, when worn, its user's body. Commodity Wi-Fi receivers report channel state information (CSI) per frame and can serve as device-referred sounders if their impairments are corrected. Synthetic ground truth reproducing a commercial receiver's impairments shows that five corrections are needed: subcarrier mapping, receive-chain order, per-packet alignment, received-signal-strength referencing, and window-response removal. Without them, the RMS delay spread reads up to 191% high, the coherence bandwidth falls to about half, or the Rician K-factor and Doppler estimates lose their meaning; with all five, the median delay-spread bias is between -6% and +14%. Applied to beacons from seven access points, including a body-worn receiver at six indoor sites at 5 and 6 GHz, the chain gives delay spreads of 24-96 ns; walking lowers the median correlation over one beacon interval from 0.85 to 0.15, near the estimator's floor. Unprecoded data frames gave 0.2-1.2 times the beacons' delay spread on the same channel, so the two should not be pooled.
entries.comment: 5 pages, 4 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation (Communication). Companion letter submitted to IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters

entries.title: AutoRSP: An AI Agent for Radar Sensing Pipeline Design
entries.abstract: Radar sensing demands a pipeline that is well-thought-out across hardware and software. We ask whether an AI agent can automatically design radar sensing pipelines at a fraction of the time, cost, and expertise that current practice needs. We present AutoRSP, an agent that embeds radar-system-level structure through sub-agents mapped to five stack layers, a code-based representation of every layer with explicitly modeled cross-layer dependencies. Feedback for the agentic search process comes from a pipeline of realistic RF simulation, on-sensor emulation, and execution on real edge devices, rather than from an LLM judge. Because such feedback can be slower than an LLM call, we present methods to efficiently optimize agentic loops. We evaluate AutoRSP on robotic imaging, automotive perception, and vital sign sensing. It produces executable pipelines with performance comparable to or better than human-expert pipelines and closed-source agents. AutoRSP's harness, tools, and benchmarks will be released to bridge the rising gap in agentic research abilities outside of frontier labs.

entries.title: First Order Real Resonant Digital Filters and A Novel Orthogonal State Generator
entries.abstract: We describe FOREST, a real, first order digital resonant filter and orthogonal state generator. We show that in spite of the imaginary nature of the roots of the transfer function of a resonator, appropriate interpretation of this transfer function nonetheless leads to a practical first order filter with real coefficients. We use a discrete state space model of FOREST to predict the resonator properties, and implement the filter in digital signal processing slices on a digital signal processing platform. Applications are in real time digital signal processing, engineering fields such as mains electricity monitoring and motor control, any application requiring a phase locked loop, and physics applications utilising high-quality-factor resonators.
entries.comment: 11 pages, 5 figures

entries.title: Doppler RaDAR Single-Frame Anomaly Detection and Consistency Assessment by Velocity-Conditioned Gaussian Spectral Modeling
entries.abstract: Reliable speed-over-ground estimation is essential for automated railway vehicles. However, the accuracy of a velocity estimate alone does not indicate whether the underlying RaDAR measurement is physically plausible. This paper introduces a velocity-conditioned Gaussian spectral modeling framework for anomaly detection and velocity consistency assessment. A neural encoder estimates the vehicle velocity from complex Doppler spectra, while a Gaussian decoder models the expected spectral distribution conditioned on a velocity estimate. Three complementary inference-time online indicators are derived: the spectral anomaly score (SAS), conditional anomaly score (CAS), and absolute velocity disagreement (AVD). Experiments demonstrate the sensitivity of the scores to velocity deviations. Under controlled spectral anomalies, SAS and CAS outperform conventional spectral indicators in most conditions. Furthermore, AVD exhibits strong correlations with actual velocity estimation errors (Pearson r>0.99) for the investigated extra-peak and local anomalies. These results demonstrate the potential of online conditional spectral modeling to assess measurement plausibility and velocity estimation reliability without requiring ground-truth velocities during inference.

entries.title: Conditional Independence Graph Learning from Dependent Data Via Time-Delay Embedding
entries.abstract: We consider the problem of inferring the conditional independence graph (CIG) of a high-dimensional stationary multivariate Gaussian time series which could be short-range dependent (SRD) or long-range dependent (LRD). In a time series graph, each component of the vector series is represented by a distinct node, and associations between components are represented by edges between the corresponding nodes. We consider a time-domain approach based on time-delay embedding, casting the problem as one of multi-attribute graph estimation for random vectors where a vector is associated with each node of the graph. For an embedding dimension d, at each node the associated (d+1)-dimensional random vector consists of a time series component and its d delayed copies, with integer delays up to d ≥1. Graph estimation from dependent data has been investigated in the past using frequency-domain methods whose analysis is restricted to SRD data. We consider a penalized negative pseudo log-likelihood function with convex lasso or non-convex regularizations to estimate the CIG. Non-convex regularization functions are log-sum, smoothly clipped absolute deviation (SCAD) and minimax concave penalty (MCP). We exploit an existing alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) approach to optimize the objective function. We establish sufficient conditions in a high-dimensional setting for consistency, local convexity when using non-convex penalties, and graph recovery, for both SRD and LRD series. We illustrate our approach with both synthetic and real-data examples. For a p-dimensional time series, the computational complexity of the ADMM algorithm is O((d+1)³ p³). Based on the numerical examples, a heuristic is suggested and illustrated for selection of d which, in theory, should tend to infinity to infer the time series graph.
entries.comment: 26 pages, 2 figures, 7 tables
entries.journalRef: J.K. Tugnait, "Conditional independence graph learning from dependent data via time-delay embedding," IEEE Access, vol. 14, pp. 169635-169661, 2026

entries.title: A Real-Time Low-Cost Platform for Non-Contact Respiratory Rate Monitoring: A Comparative Evaluation of RGB Optical Flow and Time-of-Flight Depth Sensing
entries.abstract: Respiratory rate (RR) is one of the earliest indicators of clinical deterioration, which makes its continuous measurement clinically valuable. In routine practice, however, RR is monitored almost exclusively with contact-based sensors, which require skin attachment, may alter natural breathing, and are poorly tolerated by vulnerable groups such as newborns and elderly patients. Non-contact sensing removes these constraints, with RGB video and depth imaging among its most accessible modalities. In this work, we present a low-cost, real-time platform based on a single multimodal sensor that provides both RGB and time-of-flight (ToF) data streams, implemented on a Raspberry Pi 5 edge device. The system integrates three RGB optical-flow pipelines, namely Farnebäck, Horn–Schunck, and Lucas–Kanade, together with a depth-based pipeline incorporating region-of-interest stabilization and distance-derived signal extraction, enabling the two modalities to be evaluated independently under the same experimental protocol. The proposed approach was evaluated on twelve healthy volunteers following a controlled protocol, including normal breathing, hyperventilation, and breath-holding, using a piezoresistive respiratory belt as a reference. RGB-based methods achieved lower RR estimation errors, with Lucas–Kanade attaining the lowest median MAE (3.83 BPM), whereas the ToF-based pipeline, although less accurate for RR estimation (median MAE 6.24 BPM), reached a higher apnea detection sensitivity (0.66 vs 0.51-0.55). These findings highlight the complementary strengths of both modalities and support their integration into unified low-cost platforms.

entries.title: Fast Fluid Antenna Multiple Access: Exact Analysis and Fixed-Aperture Asymptotics
entries.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the interference-limited outage performance of fast fluid antenna multiple access (FAMA), in which the receive port is selected according to the instantaneous symbol-based signal-to-interference energy ratio. For any positive-definite spatial covariance matrix and an arbitrary finite number of candidate ports, we show that constant-modulus multiuser interference admits an exact reduction to the comparison of two independent correlated exponential random vectors. This representation leads to a nonnegative double multi-index series for the outage probability, a recursive coefficient evaluation, and a certified truncation-error bound. We then study the distinct asymptotic regime where the number of candidate ports goes to infinity while the physical aperture remains unchanged, assuming exponential spatial correlation. For this model, we derive an explicit finite-port series requiring no numerical integration, and characterize continuous port selection through a convergent one-dimensional series for arbitrary thresholds. The analysis further yields an exact expression relating the maximum supportable number of users to the antenna aperture size and target outage probability. Numerical results validate the finite-port and asymptotic analyses, and illustrate that given sufficient aperture size, a user utilizing fast FAMA can overcome a massive number of interferers for decent communication performance.

entries.title: Scaled Coordinate Descent for Convex Quadratic Programs
entries.abstract: We study a modification of coordinate descent for unconstrained symmetric positive definite quadratic programs that combines a coordinate correction with an exact scaling of the current iterate. For a selected coordinate, the method minimizes the objective function over the two-dimensional subspace spanned by the current iterate and the corresponding standard basis vector. Closed-form expressions are obtained for the two update parameters and for the resulting objective decrease. The scaling produces a state-dependent effective curvature that is no larger than the diagonal curvature used by standard coordinate descent, so the exact scaled update makes at least as much progress for the same selected coordinate. We discuss initialization, numerical stability, randomized coordinate selection, experimental comparisons with ordinary two-coordinate descent, and a block coordinate extension. In the spirit of previous theoretical results, we give a probabilistic linear convergence result. Finally, we provide experimental results to show the effectiveness of the proposed method on synthetic data.
entries.comment: Papers submitted for journal consideration in September 2026

entries.title: Exact Error Analysis of Noise-Domain OTFS with Paired Covariance Signaling
entries.abstract: Noise-domain orthogonal time frequency space (ND-OTFS) encodes bits through opposite correlations in Gaussian delay–Doppler pairs of equal average energy. This letter derives the exact conditional bit error probability (BEP) of maximum-likelihood detection using generalized covariance eigenvalues and characteristic-function inversion. For scalar channels, we obtain an incomplete-beta expression and its finite-sum Rayleigh average. Partial correlation yields an error floor for a fixed observation count. At unit correlation, the conditional BEP decays with an signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) exponent equal to the number of pair observations, and common Rayleigh fading yields diversity order one. Simulations validate the analysis and quantify pair-placement effects.
entries.comment: 5 pages

entries.title: Certified Outage Bounds for RIS-Assisted NOMA with Source-Side Thermal Energy Harvesting
entries.abstract: Gaussian useful-gain and mean-interference approximations can cause opposite power-sizing errors in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). We extend a source-side thermal energy harvesting model with Poisson interference and certify two-sided outage bounds. In a tested environment, the combined required signal-to-noise ratio error has opposite signs at 20 and 24 elements per user. Under another power convention, mean or moment-matched Gamma-distributed interference can predict false feasibility with exact useful gain. In the Gamma case, the Gaussian gain approximation can mask this false feasibility. Propagated Chernoff bounds give sufficient designs. Results concern the specified model and tested regimes.
entries.comment: 5 pages, 1 figure. Submitted to IEEE Wireless Communications Letters. Code and data: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24450534

entries.title: Detecting Transmit Precoding in Commodity Wi-Fi Channel State Information and Its Effect on Measured Channel Statistics
entries.abstract: Channel state information (CSI) from commodity Wi-Fi receivers is increasingly used to estimate delay spread and fading. For multi-stream data frames, the access point may apply transmit beamforming, and the CSI then describes the precoded channel HQ instead of the propagation channel H. This letter gives a blind test for eigen-beamforming based on the near-orthogonality and power ordering of the stream columns, evaluated at the receive-chain gain ratio that minimizes their coherence. The test needs no calibration or packet alignment, tolerates gain changes between sounding and data frames, and builds on the Beta(1,N_r-1) law of the squared column coherence under unprecoded Rayleigh fading. Simulations with compressed feedback, subcarrier grouping, feedback delay, antenna correlation, and SNRs of 10-30 dB give false-alarm rates of at most 2.9×10⁻³ at the chosen thresholds and show precoding scales the per-entry RMS delay spread by factors of 0.3 to 5.7. The per-subcarrier Gram matrix HH^H is preserved: the Frobenius norm is unchanged with two transmit antennas and within 1.7 dB (95th percentile) with four. With two generations of commercial access points at 5 and 6 GHz, 880 of the 896 two-stream data frames they sent to the client tested as precoded, including 601 of 605 IEEE 802.11be frames without a beamforming flag. A third access point gave 0 of 5221 in 802.11n mode and 4003 of 5225 flagged frames in 802.11ac mode, fewer in motion; a fourth gave 3283 of 3296 with beamforming on and 0 of 3223 with it off.
entries.comment: 5 pages (4 pages and a page of references), 3 figures, 3 tables. Submitted to IEEE Antennas and Wireless Propagation Letters

entries.title: Robust Adaptive Channel Estimation for RIS-Assisted mmWave Massive MIMO via a Stochastic Shannon Entropy Criterion
entries.abstract: Accurate channel estimation in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted millimeter-wave (mmWave) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems remains challenging due to the passive nature of the RIS, the high dimensionality of the cascaded channel, and the presence of non-Gaussian impulsive disturbances. This paper proposes a robust sparsity-aware adaptive estimator, termed reweighted zero-attracting stochastic Shannon entropy (RZA-SSE), for angular-domain channel estimation. The algorithm combines a double-window kernel-based Shannon entropy criterion with a norm-normalized ℓ₁ penalty. Both the data-driven term and the nonsmooth penalty are differentiated using exact Wirtinger calculus. An exact weight-error recursion and a mean-square energy relation are derived. Local stability is analyzed via a joint coefficient–penalty state representation, and an approximate steady-state mean-square deviation (MSD) expression is obtained. Extensive simulations under Gaussian-mixture impulsive noise demonstrate that ZA-SSE consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art benchmarks in steady-state MSD.

entries.title: Domain-Generalizable Semantic Communications With Pilot-Assisted Adaptation over Wireless Channels
entries.abstract: Semantic communication offers a promising approach to support intelligent services in next-generation wireless networks by efficiently transmitting task-relevant information. However, its performance can degrade significantly when input data and wireless channel conditions differ from those encountered during training. In this paper, we propose a robust semantic communication framework that addresses these distributional mismatches through two independent but complementary modules. At the transmitter, a domain-generalization module extracts task-relevant features while suppressing domain-specific information. At the receiver, a pilot-assisted channel characterization module extracts channel context from received pilot signals to guide semantic recovery under varying wireless conditions. Through the end-to-end training of semantic encoder-decoder pair with domain alignment and channel adaptation models, the proposed framework improves task performance under simultaneous input and channel distribution shifts with limited transmitter-receiver coordination during deployment. Simulation results show that the proposed framework improves classification accuracy by more than 18% over a conventional semantic communication baseline in the unseen scenarios.

entries.title: Symbol-Level Precoding With Microwave Linear Analog Computers (MiLACs): Performance Limits and Stem-Connected Hardware Design
entries.abstract: Symbol-level precoding (SLP) improves multiuser transmission by exploiting constructive interference based on user symbols. A microwave linear analog computer (MiLAC) maps a reduced number of radio-frequency (RF) port input signals to a large antenna array through a tunable passive microwave network. Their combination enables MiLAC to reduce the RF-chain burden of SLP, while SLP offers symbol-dependent design flexibility that can alleviate the performance loss caused by a limited number of RF chains and practical circuit constraints of MiLAC. This work investigates the joint design of SLP and MiLAC and analyzes how a limited number of RF chains and practical circuit constraints affect performance. For ideal MiLAC networks, we characterize the condition for attaining fully digital SLP performance and quantify the associated performance loss otherwise. We propose the joint effective subspace MiLAC-SLP (JES-MiLAC-SLP) algorithm to jointly optimize the analog beamforming matrix and SLP signals over a symbol block. For stem-connected MiLAC networks with finite tuning ranges and quantized tuning states, we propose the hardware-constrained JES-MiLAC-SLP (HC-JES-MiLAC-SLP) algorithm. It identifies circuit state changes for which SLP can better compensate the errors caused by circuit limitations, and updates the circuit state accordingly. Numerical results validate the derived findings and show that joint design reduces errors relative to separate MiLAC and SLP designs. Under the considered configurations, HC-JES-MiLAC-SLP substantially narrows the gap to fully digital SLP.

entries.title: Geometry-Time Graph Attention for 3-D TOA Localization in Underwater Acoustic Sensor Networks
entries.abstract: In underwater acoustic sensor networks, depth-dependent variations in sound speed refract acoustic rays, complicating the estimation of target positions from travel-time measurements. Propagation-model-based methods rely on an assumed or estimated sound speed profile (SSP), and a mismatch between that profile and the current environment can bias position estimates. To address this limitation, this paper proposes an underwater graph attention network (UGAN) that fuses synchronized time-of-arrival (TOA) observations from multiple stations with reference-station coordinates to estimate three-dimensional target positions without requiring the current sound speed profile at inference. UGAN constructs one graph per target for batch inference. Its geometry–time attention mechanism combines interstation geometry with ordered pairs of TOA observations to compute attention weights in all three graph layers and enrich the messages in the last two layers. A shared nonlinear encoder supplies individual TOA features directly to every layer. In ray-tracing simulations with a fixed five-station deployment and two SSPs held out from training and validation, UGAN achieves mean localization root mean square errors (RMSE) of 0.307, 0.577, and 0.989 m at three increasing TOA noise levels, representing reductions of 52.0%, 31.0%, and 22.8% relative to the evaluated GATv2 baseline, respectively. At the intermediate noise level, incorporating station-pair relations into the messages reduces the mean localization RMSE by 9.4% with relation-based attention scoring enabled. For 4,000 target observations, UGAN takes a median of 58.14 ms on the same GPU, 7.0% less time than GATv2.

entries.title: Subspace-Coding for Bistatic ISAC: Taming Interference via Array Geometry
entries.abstract: This paper introduces a subspace coding perspective to bistatic integrated sensing and communication (ISAC), highlighting the role of receiver array geometry in the coupling between communication decoding and sensing. A central insight is that the impact of the interference caused by the sensing channel on the line-of-sight communication path is controlled by the subspace distance between the sensing and communication subspaces, which strongly depends on the array geometry. By studying a commonly used successive decoding approach, we derive upper and lower bounds on the communication error probability in terms of an effective SINR, which is explicitly determined by this subspace distance. This reveals that array geometries designed to form well-separated sensing subspace codes can also improve communication reliability in bistatic ISAC. In particular, Bose–Chowla arrays, shown to be near-optimal subspace codes for spatial sensing in our earlier works, can outperform uniform linear arrays in terms of symbol decoding errors. The performance gap is significant when the communication and sensing channels are strongly correlated, and it increases with the number of antennas. Numerical experiments confirm that subspace-coded array geometries provide more favorable sensing–communication tradeoffs than ULAs for iterative joint target localization and decoding (JTD) receiver.
entries.comment: Accepted for publication in the Proceedings of IEEE ISAC 2026

entries.title: ClusterVAD: Threshold-Free Unsupervised Voice Activity Detection with Pre-Trained Neural Representations
entries.abstract: Voice activity detection (VAD) is one of the first steps in speech processing pipelines, from transcription and diarization to speech language models. Supervised detectors need labelled data and inherit the domain and annotation conventions of their training corpora. Existing unsupervised detectors rely on hand-crafted acoustic features which cannot benefit from data and degrade in far-field, noisy or atypical speech. We propose ClusterVAD, an unsupervised VAD built on frozen speech foundation model representations. Fitted once on a small set of untranscribed speech, it clusters the representations and labels each cluster as speech or non-speech with sonority, an acoustic measure. At inference, a frame-level speech probability is computed from the cluster assignments, and a two-state hidden Markov model fitted to each recording enables threshold-free detection. Across benchmarks covering meetings, far-field and noisy recordings, Mandarin and dysarthric speech, ClusterVAD obtains the lowest detection error on pause-level references and is competitive on speaker turn-level references. These results indicate that speech foundation models inherently capture the distinction between speech and non-speech, which can be leveraged without training a detector.

entries.title: SHARPnP: Self-Supervised and Plug-and-Play Hyperspectral Super-Resolution from Real Noisy Unaligned Camera Measurements
entries.abstract: Affordable snapshot hyperspectral cameras capture spectral images in a single exposure but suffer from limited spatial resolution and sensor noise. Low-cost RGB cameras provide fine visible details to guide NIR reconstruction, but introduce spatially varying cross-camera misalignment. Supervised fusion methods require relatively large datasets of clean, high-resolution hyperspectral images, are sensitive to sensor noise, and generalize poorly across new sensors. We introduce SHARPnP, an interpretable, flexible framework coupling registration and reconstruction for RGB-guided hyperspectral super-resolution from noisy, unaligned measurements without clean references. We adapt a pretrained registration model via a cross-view loss backpropagated through a fixed plug-and-play fusion module. Temporal and recorrupted pairs enable reference-free self-supervision on noisy inputs. At test time, we calibrate cross-camera radiometry and refine alignment. Plug-and-play fusion employs sequential three-band denoising. On the REAL benchmark, SHARPnP outperforms supervised fusion baselines at 4×, 8×, and 16× on clean inputs and at 4× under Gaussian noise (σ=5/255, 10/255). On native RGB-HSI snapshot measurements, it reconstructs all 51 VIS-NIR bands, beyond the conventional 31-band VIS setting, without high-resolution references.

entries.title: Score-Based Diffusion for Hypergraph Signals in the t-Spectral Domain
entries.abstract: We introduce the first score-based generative model for signals on a fixed hypergraph, formulated in the spectral domain of t-product hypergraph signal processing (t-HGSP). The naive tensor heat semigroup is ill-posed, since after palindromic symmetrization the spectral slices of the Laplacian tensor are no longer positive semidefinite. A per-mode frequency shift repairs it, yielding a forward Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion that decouples per (eigenmode, slice) pair with closed-form marginals, exact score targets, and an exactly isotropic stationary law. A lightweight slice-conditioned denoiser is trained on the resulting real spectral grid. Sampling combines its score on data-active modes with the closed-form score elsewhere, which proves essential for stability at scale. A closed cosine-form observation operator turns missing-node recovery into linear-Gaussian guidance with stabilized posterior sampling. On hypergraphs of up to 500 nodes, our model beats a clique-expansion baseline by margins growing from 2× to 27× in covariance error, matches the graph-spectral statistics of the data better than the graph-basis model itself, and reaches the finite-sample estimation floor on data rotated off the t-spectral axes. Posterior sampling reduces missing-node NMSE to 0.28-0.64 (classical baselines 0.87-1.1) at conservative coverage, and cuts the framework's own denoising baseline by up to 3.6×.
entries.comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to ICASSP 2027

entries.title: QoS-Constrained Sum-Rate Maximization in RIS-Assisted Pinching-Antenna NOMA Systems
entries.abstract: This paper investigates a two-user downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) system jointly assisted by a single-waveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) and a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS). To maximize the achievable sum rate under quality-of-service (QoS) constraints, the pinching antenna (PA) positions, RIS phase shifts, and power allocation coefficients are jointly optimized. The resulting non-convex optimization problem is addressed using an alternating optimization (AO) framework, where power allocation is obtained in closed form, while RIS phase shifts and PA positions are optimized through majorization-minimization (MM) and sequential quadratic programming (SQP), respectively. Numerical results show that the proposed architecture achieves higher sum rates than conventional-antenna and PASS-only benchmarks. Moreover, the MM- and SQP-based optimization stages achieve performance comparable to semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and grid-based exhaustive search, respectively, while the AO algorithm exhibits rapid convergence.

entries.title: Embodied Intelligence for Spectrum Map Construction in Low-Altitude Wireless Networks
entries.abstract: Accurate spectrum map construction by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) is crucial for intelligent resource management in low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs). Although various construction approaches have been investigated, their performance often degrades under extremely sparse sampling because purely data-driven models may not capture the underlying propagation physics. To address these challenges, an embodied intelligence framework is proposed, which synergistically integrates closed-loop perception-cognition-execution (PCE) coupling and embodied exploration to achieve precise and efficient spectrum construction. Based on this framework, a corresponding embodied cognition and decision network (ECDNet) with three tightly coupled modules is designed. Specifically, by leveraging distance-aware convolutions, the semantic bridge, and adaptive feature alignment mechanisms, ECDNet establishes the bidirectional information flow between construction and decision-making. Simulation results show that ECDNet achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) of 2.787 dBm at 4.00% sampling under the non-revisiting spiral protocol. Furthermore, a practical UAV-based spectrum construction platform is developed and field-deployed to provide prototype-level evidence that the sensing, cognition, and action modules execute as a closed loop on size, weight, and power constrained UAV edge devices.
entries.comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 4 tables. Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Mobile Computing

entries.title: Low-Power Spiking Neural Network Acceleration with Differential Time Representation: A Modular Hardware Framework
entries.abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer promising energy efficiency, making them well suited for energy-constrained applications. Much of their energy savings stems from the sparse encoding of spike trains. We show that spike trains can be represented more efficiently using Differential Time Representation (DTR), which requires fewer bits than Address-Event Representation (AER) or equidistantly sampled 1-bit spike trains. To support multiple input spike trains, we provide a rigorous proof that DTR sequences can be merged with low complexity. We also provide a set of modular hardware streaming components using this representation that can be flexibly connected to construct custom accelerator architectures for specific SNNs. Tailoring the hardware architecture to the selected SNN is streamlined by a Python framework combining the modular hardware components into a full SNN implementation. We use the framework to generate three accelerators for the Spiking Heidelberg Digits (SHD), Spiking Speech Commands (SSC), and PSMNIST benchmarks, each in a throughput-optimized parallel variant and a resource-reduced time-multiplexed variant. We report results for FPGA and ASIC implementations, the latter synthesized with a fully open-source flow targeting the predictive ASAP7 PDK. On the SHD dataset, the ASIC implementation reaches 92.46% classification accuracy, while sustaining ≈12,027 inferences per second at 20.37μJ per inference, exceeding the neuromorphic Loihi processor by 109× in throughput and 1.8× in energy efficiency. The corresponding FPGA implementation achieves ≈6,023 inferences per second without using DSP blocks. Across all three datasets, the synthesized ASICs reduce energy per inference by 27-37× relative to their FPGA counterparts, demonstrating that competitive SNN accelerators can be realized entirely within an open-source design flow.

entries.title: Robust inverse dielectric design of skin phantoms for implantable wireless link evaluation
entries.abstract: Skin phantoms support reproducible evaluation of implantable wireless links, yet published complex permittivities of skin predict different propagation losses. We formulate a robust inverse design to determine a homogeneous phantom permittivity that minimizes the largest channel-loss difference across selected skin reference models, incidence angles and both transverse-electric and transverse-magnetic polarizations. Computed candidates and analytical lower bounds bracket the optimal mismatch and constrain the critical depth. Across seven frequencies from 5 to 500 GHz, the minimax mismatch at 1.3 mm ranges from 1.13 to 13.72 dB. For a 3 dB tolerance, suitable permittivities exist at every investigated depth at 5 GHz, while critical depths at the other frequencies range from 0.23 to 1.01 mm. Only one of seven material cases from the literature meets a 6 dB tolerance at 1.3 mm. These results translate channel-loss tolerances into quantitative design criteria for skin phantoms used in implantable wireless link evaluation.

entries.title: A Hybrid Analytical-Neural Residual Surrogate for Fast Radio Propagation Prediction over Irregular Terrain
entries.abstract: Fast prediction of radio-wave propagation over irregular terrain is important for coverage analysis in mountainous environments, where many terrain and antenna configurations must be evaluated repeatedly. High-fidelity split-step parabolic equation (SSPE) solvers can capture terrain-induced shadowing and interference, but their computational cost is high for repeated planning studies. Learning-based surrogates reduce this cost, but direct field regression asks the network to learn both analytically tractable propagation trends and terrain-dependent residual structure. This paper proposes a hybrid analytical-neural residual surrogate that separates these two parts. A deterministic analytical baseline represents free-space spreading, antenna directivity, modified knife-edge diffraction, and terrain-aware specular reflection, while a compact coarse-to-fine neural network predicts the residual field. The network uses baseline-derived guidance channels, anisotropic convolutions, and feature-wise antenna conditioning to match the directional structure of terrain propagation fields. On synthetic SSPE data at 1.0 GHz, the proposed model achieves an MAE of 2.1061 dB, compared with 3.3955 dB for a standard U-Net and 3.2560 dB for a reproduced physics-guided CNN, while reducing the average inference time to 11.30 ms per sample. A zero-shot test at 1.8 GHz gives an MAE of 2.8692 dB without retraining, and a case study on the measured Hjorringvej terrain profile shows that the prediction remains consistent with the SSPE reference and follows the measured path-loss trend.
entries.comment: Under review at IEEE Transactions on Antennas and Propagation

entries.title: Multiple-Input Multiple-Output Forward Scatter Radar
entries.abstract: Forward Scatter Radar (FSR) enhances the detection of low-observable targets by exploiting the increased radar cross section that occurs when a target crosses the transmitter-receiver baseline. Conventional FSR typically uses single-input single-output (SISO) architectures with limited localization capability, while recent single-input multiple-output (SIMO) systems enable non-coherent angular estimation. This paper introduces a multiple-input multiple-output FSR (MIMO-FSR) framework for joint estimation of target direction of departure (DoD) and direction of arrival (DoA) from non-coherent, amplitude-only measurements. By exploiting antenna arrays at both the transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX), the proposed approach enables two-dimensional angular localization without phase synchronization among TX/RX array elements. We establish the underlying operating principle under ideal signal separability and then develop practical frequency-division multiplexing (FDM) and time-division multiplexing (TDM) implementations. For each scheme, dedicated signal models and processing methods compensate for distortions caused by frequency offsets and target motion, respectively. We also derive analytical expressions for angular resolution, ambiguity conditions, and output-map distortions. Extensive numerical simulations for short- and long-baseline scenarios reveal operational limits and trade-offs between the two multiplexing schemes. Finally, proof-of-concept outdoor experiments using software-defined radio platforms validate the proposed framework. The results demonstrate joint DoD-DoA estimation and support the feasibility of MIMO-FSR for future active, passive, and integrated sensing and communications applications.

entries.title: Waveform Randomization for Secure ISAC Against Informed Eavesdroppers
entries.abstract: We study waveform-level protection of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) against a UAV-mounted eavesdropper (Eve) that knows the waveform construction and the phase-key generation rules. The novelty of this work is a systematic, budget-explicit attack analysis: instead of relying on undisclosed design details, we quantify what an informed Eve can learn and reconstruct, and how much computation this takes. We protect the sensing reference with Fourier-curve modulation, phase keys, and tangent Artificial Noise (AN), with burst- specific information shared over secure backhaul. We compare three key-generation rules against offline Convolutional Neural Network (CNN)-based sequence identification and online Adam and phase-aware expectation-maximization (EM) key recovery, under complete or partial nominal-sequence knowledge. A power- domain model couples residual key error with imperfect AN removal and predicts coherent delay locking. Results show that reusable key structure permits sequence identification even when demodulation fails, position-dependent keying raises recovery difficulty, and seed-expanded keying resists the evaluated clas- sifier within the learning budget. Waveform simulations under multipath, clutter, and echo accumulation confirm the sensing impact.
entries.comment: Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Communication

entries.title: Interference-Free In-Symbol Pilots for High-Mobility DFT-s-OFDM Uplink
entries.abstract: The 5G New Radio (NR) uplink uses discrete Fourier transform spread orthogonal frequency-division multi- plexing (DFT-s-OFDM) for its low peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). Its demodulation reference signal (DMRS) occupies whole symbols, although channel estimation only needs channel samples. Since existing designs cannot place pilots inside a data symbol without interference on the data, or on both data and pilots, NR keeps whole DMRS symbols, which wastes spectral efficiency (SE), and adds more of them as the channel varies faster, lowering the SE further. We develop a technique that places pilots free of data interference inside the data symbols, for frequency-domain channel estimation in every symbol. Using the Zak transform, we show that leaving a set of equally spaced pre- DFT samples empty frees one column of the Zak grid of the DFT output. The data values of the pilot subcarriers are relocated into this column by adding a constant over a few subcarrier combs, which preserves the energy and keeps the NR DFT sizes. The receiver undoes it linearly with comb sums, without decisions or side information, and a symbol loses as few as one data sample beyond its pilots. Since the pilots raise the PAPR, we keep them few per symbol and hop their positions across symbols, so that a two-dimensional estimator over the slot resolves long delay spreads at high Doppler. On 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP) channels, pilots in every symbol achieve a higher effective SE than all NR DMRS configurations from pedestrian to high- speed-train velocities, at a PAPR close to plain DFT-s-OFDM.
entries.comment: 10 pages, 8 figures

entries.title: Dual-Pilot Design for OCDM Channel Estimation
entries.abstract: Channel acquisition in orthogonal chirp division multiplexing (OCDM) over doubly-dispersive channels incurs a large pilot overhead, since delay and Doppler jointly shift the symbols in the chirp domain and separating them requires repeated pilots, each protected against the complete coupled displacement. This letter proposes a dual-pulsone pilot design that reduces this overhead in two steps. First, a pulsone occupies fewer chirp-domain bins than alias-free Doppler estimation requires, deliberately allowing Doppler wrapping. Second, a phase-offset pulsone is placed within the same protected region to observe a complementary part of the displacement, further reducing the shared guard. The phase offset also resolves the wrapping ambiguity, enabling low-complexity delay-Doppler estimation. Simulations show competitive estimation and BER performance, with the lowest complexity and highest payload efficiency among the considered OCDM estimators.
entries.comment: 5 pages, 6 figures

entries.title: Sequences for Flat-Top Beams
entries.abstract: Flat-top beams have numerous applications in radar and communication systems. Sequences with diverging merit factors can approach the ideal omnidirectional beams but do not directly apply to flat-top beams, which require simultaneous control of passband ripple and stopband leakage. To bridge this gap, we study the asymptotic behavior of both quantities of flat-top beams by using tools of Fourier analysis. We establish contrasting results for sequences with finite or infinite alphabets. For sequences with finite alphabet, including binary and quaternary ones, their passband ripple and stopband leakage cannot simultaneously vanish as the sequence length grows to infinity. For sequences with infinite alphabet, however, both requirements are satisfied simultaneously by the generalized step-chirp (GSC) sequences if and only if the length-bandwidth product Nγ goes to infinity and the distance of the step size a from {0,1,12,13,…} goes to zero. Besides, both quantities vanish at rate O((Nγ)^(-1/2)) if a∈{1,12,13,…}.These results broaden the scope of classical sequence design beyond full-band spectral flatness and provide a theoretical foundation for flat-top beam synthesis.

entries.title: DBFM: Dual-Band Flow Matching for ECG Super-Resolution
entries.abstract: Long-term ECG monitoring is increasingly supported by wearable and portable devices, where limited power and transmission capacity motivate acquisition at lower sampling rates. ECG super-resolution (SR) aims to reconstruct high-sampling-rate signals from low-sampling-rate recordings for clinical analysis. A recent diffusion-based approach, DiSR-ECG, has demonstrated powerful reconstruction performance, particularly in cross-dataset evaluation. However, its iterative sampling during inference incurs high computational cost when processing large volumes of long-term ECG data. To reduce this cost while maintaining reconstruction accuracy, we propose Dual-Band Flow Matching (DBFM), a generative framework for ECG SR. DBFM decomposes ECG signals into low- and high-frequency components and separately learns their source-to-target transport using conditional flow matching. This dual-band formulation enables frequency-specific reconstruction, while one-step inference substantially reduces computational complexity. Experimental results show that DBFM achieves performance comparable to or better than DiSR-ECG while reducing inference FLOPs by approximately 98.7%. These results demonstrate that DBFM enables computationally efficient ECG SR without compromising reconstruction quality.

entries.title: Integrated Semantic Sensing and Communications: Target Attribute Inference and Beamforming Design
entries.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) is expected to become a key enabling paradigm for future 6G networks, supporting emerging applications that require a comprehensive understanding of sensed targets. As a step toward this goal, we consider an ISAC system with semantic sensing capability that determines what the sensed target is, where it is located, and how large it is. However, the accurate retrieval of these attributes, including target class, location, and size, is challenging due to the highly nonlinear relationships between the received signals and different attributes. In addition, new beamforming strategies are also required to balance multi-user communication and semantic sensing performance. To address the first challenge, we develop a physics-guided inference model that leverages signal propagation priors and a unified Transformer backbone to effectively characterize the highly nonlinear relationships between received ISAC signals and multiple attributes. As for the second challenge, we develop a multi-stage training framework for the optimization of beamformers and model parameters, aiming to improve semantic sensing performance while guaranteeing multi-user communication requirements. Simulation results show that under the same multi-user communication rate requirements, the proposed scheme can provide more than 12% performance gains across classification, localization, and size estimation tasks compared with existing methods and achieve 91.21% classification accuracy using only two OFDM frames, demonstrating the feasibility of accurate semantic sensing with low measurement overhead.

entries.title: CRISP: Sparse Risk-Calibrated Front-End Allocation and Fusion for Low-Resolution Snapshot GNSS Positioning
entries.abstract: Low-resolution global navigation satellite system snapshot receivers face strong coupling among automatic gain control compression, coarse quantization, and waveform distortion from nonlinear interference mitigation. This paper presents Cross-Risk Interference-Resilient Snapshot Positioning, denoted CRISP, an aided single-snapshot architecture that allocates and fuses complementary pre-correlation processors over a bounded position-clock search region under a shared direct position estimation solve budget. On a pre-frozen baseband descriptor partition, offline calibration estimates uncentered second-order position-error cross moments and solves cardinality-constrained simplex programs along east, north, and up axes, retaining validation-screened multibranch combinations while assigning single matched processors elsewhere. An online reliability gate screens the same quantized snapshot to route unfamiliar waveforms toward single-branch protective operators. We characterize profiled contrast shifts after nonlinear suppression and derive a conditional finite-sample excess-risk bound across disjoint splits alongside an exact same-snapshot gating risk identity. Across 17 568 simulated 2-ms GPS L1 C/A trials, CRISP reduces core positioning root-mean-square error by 13.84%, > 100-m gross errors by 41.32%, and multi-geometry error by 12.23% over Snapshot-FD at 1.43 core and 1.51 overall solves per snapshot.

entries.title: Net-Gain-Optimized Constellation Shaping for the 5G NR DFT-s-OFDM Uplink: Probabilistic, Geometric, and Joint Designs
entries.abstract: Constellation shaping improves the achievable information rate of coded modulation. On the single-carrier uplink waveform of 5G New Radio, discrete Fourier transform (DFT)- spread orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM), the same shaping can also raise the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). A higher PAPR forces more power amplifier back- off and reduces the link budget. Prior work characterized this penalty for fixed probabilistically and geometrically shaped constellations, but did not turn the trade-off into a design objective. We optimize constellation shaping (CS) to maximize the net-gain, i.e., the sum of the communication gain and the PAPR gain, at the fixed spectral efficiency of 4 bits per channel use for 64-QAM. We apply it to probabilistic shaping (PS), geometric shaping (GS), and a joint scheme that combines both. As the coded block error rate cannot be evaluated inside a gradient loop, we use the achievable information rate as a surrogate for the communication performance and the PAPR surrogate as differentiable cost functions for the optimizer. The learned constellations are then validated on a complete DFT-s-OFDM link-level chain. Conventional Maxwell-Boltzmann PS yields a negative net-gain, but net-gain-aware optimization removes this deficit in every method. GS converts it into a substantial gain, as it not only improves the communication performance but also lowers the PAPR below the uniform 64-QAM reference, achieving the largest net-gain among the CS methods studied.
entries.comment: Submitted to WCNC2027

entries.title: Strategic Beam Brainstorming for Generative Site-Specific Beamforming
entries.abstract: A novel plug-and-play candidate beam selection strategy is proposed for generative site-specific beamforming (GenSSBF), a paradigm that draws on a learned conditional channel distribution to generate multiple plausible beams. Under a limited probing budget, realizing the full potential of GenSSBF requires identifying which candidate beams are worth probing. To this end, the marginal probing value is first derived to guide strategic candidate probing by quantifying each beam's additional gain beyond those already selected. Based on this criterion, two algorithms are developed without retraining the generator: 1) Greedy candidate probing (GCP) selects all candidate beams from a locally generated pool prior to over-the-air probing, requiring only a single feedback round; 2) Adaptive candidate probing (ACP) exploits reference signal received power (RSRP) feedback after each probe to update channel hypothesis weights and guide the next beam selection, without increasing the asymptotic complexity. Simulations across three ray-tracing scenarios under noiseless and noisy probing reveal that: 1) candidate complementarity is key to efficient beam brainstorming; and 2) ACP is particularly beneficial when initial sensing leaves substantial channel uncertainty and subsequent feedback is reliable.

entries.title: PhysRF-WorldJEPA: Transforming Heterogeneous Large Language Models into Manifold-Decoupled Millimeter-Wave Radar World Models
entries.abstract: Adapting Large Language Models (LLMs) to millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar enables privacy-preserving, all-weather physical scene understanding across darkness, smoke, and walls. However, standard instruction tuning treats continuous radar streams as static text-like tokens, causing near-random global radar-to-text retrieval and severe physical drift under sensor blackouts. Conversely, coupling pairwise contrastive losses (e.g., SigLIP) directly into the shared backbone improves retrieval but injects O(B²) repulsive gradients that fracture continuous coordinate manifolds (R² < 0). We present PhysRF-WorldJEPA, a manifold-decoupled Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) that separates continuous electromagnetic state prediction from cross-modal language alignment. An unattenuated 1.0x clock anchor and parallel dual-scale RF encoder feed a lean ~3% LoRA LLM trained with two-step state-space EMA-JEPA (Denoise -> Rollout) and sample-axis Batch-VICReg to predict +3.0 s physical states; a stop-gradient alignment head then maps frozen prompt states onto the text hypersphere with false-negative masking. On a 4,541-window tri-domain suite (77/60.25/60 GHz) against 10 baselines, freezing the physical backbone and training only the decoupled head lifts R->T R@10 from 5.95% to 15.01% and improves MedRank from 107.0 to 60.0 while preserving identical physical readout: 3.37 deg (R²=+0.961) blackout +3.0 s torso tilt, 1.89 m (R²=+0.679; 1.19 m/+0.863 at the RF front-end) cluttered UAV altitude, 2.04 m (R²=+0.461) behind-wall NLOS range, 0.9976 virtual-RIS invariance, and 100% fall recall. Across five 0.5B-1.8B LLM families (15 zero-overhead models), World-JEPA improves retrieval and 75%-drop completion in 10/10 runs and blackout tilt in 4/5 (Span-Euc), 2/5 (Scatter), and 5/5 (per-family best) over SFT.
entries.comment: 11 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables

entries.title: Wireless-OptSG: A Versatile Multi-Agent Optimization Framework for Wireless Resource Allocation
entries.abstract: 6G wireless networks are expected to accommodate heterogeneous service requirements across diverse deployment scenarios, giving rise to physical-layer resource allocation problems with scenario-dependent objectives and constraints. Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and agent systems can interpret wireless-domain specifications and incorporate execution feedback into optimization. However, translating language-level reasoning into feasible, high-quality resource allocations remains challenging, since candidates need to satisfy precise mathematical constraints throughout iterative search. This work proposes the Wireless Optimization Solution Generator (Wireless-OptSG), a versatile multi-agent framework for physical-layer resource allocation. Wireless-OptSG organizes optimization as a feedback-driven candidate search guided by a static meta-prompt and an evolving optimization history. In a nested outer-inner loop, parallel agents explore solution trajectories and periodically exchange high-quality records to guide candidate generation. Feasible initialization uses executable optimization primitives, while a tiered repair pipeline restores feasibility and solution-dependent context improves retained-record informativeness. Experiments on four representative tasks under perfect and imperfect channel state information show that Wireless-OptSG achieves performance comparable to scenario-specific state-of-the-art (SOTA) solvers, exceeds SOTA in some settings, and consistently outperforms generic baselines, demonstrating its potential as a transferable optimization framework for future wireless networks.
entries.comment: 13 pages, 8 figures, 4 tables

entries.title: EEGJev: A System One Decision Model and Benchmark for Multi-Task EEG Question Answering
entries.abstract: A single electroencephalographic (EEG) recording can support multiple decoding tasks. Fixed-label tests cannot show how EEG foundation models handle changing questions or options. We introduce EEGJev, a fast decision model that scores candidate answers in one pass. Our benchmark, EEGJev-Bench, covers six question types across 19 public EEG sources. We held the recording and options fixed while switching between questions about attributes paired during training, such as facial expression and the hand participants were asked to use. Across 13 test sources, EEGJev selected a label for the requested attribute with 99.70% accuracy (49.20% under uniform choice). Balanced accuracy for the specific answer was 62.04%. Its 95th-percentile response time was shorter than NeuroLM's on matched validation questions answered individually. EEGJev lets users switch decoding targets by changing the question. With EEGJev-Bench, researchers can test whether new decoders follow the question more reliably, identify the correct answer more often, or both.
entries.comment: 28 pages, 6 figures. Includes supplementary information

entries.title: Model Order Detection with Parameter Estimation Guarantees for the Matrix Pencil Method
entries.abstract: Detecting the model order and estimating the parameters of sums of damped complex exponentials in noise is challenging when poles are closely spaced, the sample size is small, or the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is low. We propose REECAP, a matrix pencil (MP) algorithm for joint model order detection and pole estimation. The algorithm computes candidate poles using an overestimated working rank and classifies them using a score derived from their associated eigenvectors. The model order is then estimated by counting the retained candidates. The score measures the eigenvector energy concentration in coordinates corresponding to the dominant right singular subspace of the data Hankel matrix. Under a suitable rank condition, we derive a deterministic sufficient condition guaranteeing that a candidate whose score exceeds a certain threshold lies within a prescribed tolerance of at least one signal pole. This establishes a theoretical connection between eigenvector energy concentration and pole-estimation accuracy. Extensive simulations demonstrate improved model order detection and frequency estimation performance relative to conventional MP order detection methods, recent structure-aware MP methods, and information-theoretic criteria (ITC), across a broad range of scenarios, including clustered frequencies, low SNR in the threshold region, and small sample sizes. Runtime comparisons further demonstrate substantial computational savings, and moderate sensitivity to noise model mismatch, compared to the evaluated structure-aware and information-theoretic methods.

entries.title: Multi-User Linear Precoder Optimization for Obfuscation-Aided Mixed Regular and Wiretap Coding
entries.abstract: Physical-layer security has attracted considerable research interest with the development of quantum computing. One prominent approach is wiretap coding, which exploits the channel advantage of a legitimate receiver over an eavesdropper to achieve secure communication. However, under unfavorable channel conditions, wiretap coding can significantly reduce the achievable rate compared to regular channel coding. Mixed coding alleviates this limitation by using wiretap coding to protect a short secret required for obfuscation, while the obfuscated payload is encoded using regular channel coding. In this work, we propose a generalized obfuscation-aided mixed-coding system based on the multi-user (MU)-linear precoding (LP) architecture that unifies existing approaches employing different obfuscation functions. We then formulate the corresponding precoder optimization problem, abstracting the obfuscation function through a minimum secrecy rate constraint. Numerical simulations using a geometric two-user line-of-sight (LoS) channel demonstrated how the minimum secrecy rate requirement determines the operating point of mixed coding between regular and wiretap coding. Subsequent beampattern analysis revealed a key synergy between mixed coding and precoding: Mixed coding enables individual beam shaping for the two coding layers. Finally, spatial analysis showed that mixed coding offers the largest sum-rate gains when users are positioned at similar angles.
entries.comment: 6 pages + 7 pages appendix, 6 figures, 3 tables, 1 algorithm. Extended version of the manuscript submitted to IEEE WCNC 2027, including the detailed derivation of the SCA algorithm

entries.title: Modeling Lunar Power Harvesting and Battery Recharging In The Presence of Random Pointing Error
entries.abstract: In our work, we establish a lunar power beaming environment between a low-lunar orbiter and a circular solar panel mounted on top of a lunar vehicle located at the Lunar South Pole. Due to the random nature of the pointing errors, various upper bounds reflecting the severity of these errors are considered. Although harvested power is modelled stochastically in the literature, we extend this randomness to battery-storage analysis by deriving PDFs of state of charge, accumulated battery capacity and energy, and end-to-end efficiency for both battery charging modes. Then, our derivations are verified with extensive Monte Carlo simulations. Hence, our derivations provide a mathematical model that enables prediction and helps us understand the randomness of the corresponding variables. For the given pointing error levels, we quantify the differences between charging modes in these battery metrics. Our work explains the stochastic nature of these battery metrics in a realistic lunar environment. Regarding the end-to-end efficiency metric, which is the ratio of the stored electrical energy to the transmitted electrical energy, we observed that slow-charging efficiency is immune to pointing errors, and this mode can utilize only one-sixth of what the link can deliver under a mild pointing error.
entries.comment: 12 pages

entries.title: A concave-convex approach to bit depth allocation for linear MMSE estimation in wireless sensor networks with correlated noise
entries.abstract: Nodes in a wireless sensor network (WSN) are generally powered by batteries, and therefore energy efficiency is crucial. The bit depth used to quantize the sensor signal samples heavily influences energy consumption, as it strongly impacts the amount of information to be transmitted between the sensor nodes. Bit depth allocation problems seek to assign a bit depth to each sensor signal to optimize network resources, such as energy or bandwidth, together with algorithmic performance. We study a general bit depth allocation problem for linear minimum mean squared error (MMSE) estimation in WSNs with spatially correlated noise and a communication energy model depending linearly on the sensor bit depths. This model follows from common configurations in digital communications with orthogonal multiple-access schemes. After relaxation to real variables, we formulate the resulting non-convex problem as a difference of convex (DC) problem, and develop an algorithm based on the concave-convex procedure (CCP) to find a local optimum. We show that the convex problem involved in each CCP iteration can be efficiently solved with a worst-case complexity that is linear in the number of sensors. Additionally, we show that our approach is more computationally efficient than previously proposed bit depth allocation algorithms and generic optimization methods, and it achieves significant energy savings.
entries.comment: 16 pages double column, 10 figures

entries.title: MSW: a Multi-Scale Sliced Wasserstein Distance Between Image Distributions
entries.abstract: We propose the multi-scale sliced Wasserstein (MSW) distance between image distributions, which operates in pixel space and requires no trained network. MSW convolves images with a fixed bank of discrete cosine filters at several scales, pools the responses over all positions, and compares the resulting one-dimensional distributions using the Wasserstein distance. We pair MSW with an exact two-sample test that gives calibrated p-values. Most metrics compare two image sets in the latent space of a pretrained network. We show that these metrics are insensitive to simple perturbations of the images, because the latent space is nearly invariant to them. In contrast, MSW detects smaller perturbations than latent-space metrics and needs far fewer images to do so. Although it uses no learned features, it still detects semantic changes of the image distribution. Finally, MSW matches or outperforms existing Wasserstein-based metrics in our experiments.

entries.title: InterGS+: Inter-Frame Gaussian Splatting Compression with Geometry-Aware Transformer Prediction and Adaptive Residual Coding
entries.abstract: Dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides real-time photorealistic rendering, but representing each frame as irregular Gaussian primitives with high-dimensional attributes creates substantial storage and transmission cost. Exploiting temporal redundancy is challenging because Gaussian primitives do not preserve fixed identities across frames. We propose InterGS+, a lightweight post-hoc inter-frame codec that jointly improves temporal prediction and residual representation. Current-frame geometry is coded with G-PCC and reconstructed before prediction, enabling consistent temporal neighborhoods at encoder and decoder. Attributes are predicted using lightweight KNN and bilateral predictors together with a geometry-aware transformer for spherical-harmonic (SH) appearance, with per-Gaussian mode selection. Residual coding is adapted to each attribute: SH innovations are coded in a shared PCA domain using vector quantization with refinement, opacity and scale in activated gamma-companded domains, and rotation as canonicalized quaternion innovations using vector quantization and refinement. On MPEG dynamic sequences, InterGS+ achieves average BD-rate reductions of 45.48% over G-PCC Amd. 1 and 7.78% over InterGS-Lite, with corresponding BD-PSNR gains of 9.98 dB and 1.10 dB. Average decoding complexity is 0.049 ms/Gaussian, demonstrating efficient streamable dynamic 3DGS compression.
entries.comment: Accepted for poster presentation at the 2027 Data Compression Conference (DCC 2027)

entries.title: Automated classification of modal displacements
entries.abstract: The bending, torsional, or coupled character of a mode shape helps determine the dynamic behaviour of aerospace and civil structures. In vibration testing, it is assigned by inspecting mode shape plots, and depends on the analyst. This work proposes four indices to describe the motion of a mode from a few sensor vectors: a bending score, a torsion score, a twist share and an in-plane ratio. They are assessed on the first eight finite element modes of a tapered plate with a swept trailing edge. They are applied to identified XB-2 wing modes and to the published modes of the Sheraton Universal Hotel, a reinforced concrete (RC) building. On the plate, the twist share separates bending, coupled and torsion modes. The XB-2 modes include one bending and three coupled modes (one dominated by in-plane bending and two by out-of-plane bending). The coupled mode dominated by in-plane bending (15.25 Hz, in-plane ratio 1.33) was not investigated in earlier campaigns on the wing. On the RC building, all five modes are bending (twist share below 0.0005). The twist share and the in-plane ratio indicate the type of each mode. Hence, modes are classified without visually inspecting the mode shapes. Code and processed data are openly released.

entries.title: Directed brain-body graphs across timescales
entries.abstract: Simultaneous brain and body recordings combine signals sampled at very different rates with processes that act on timescales from milliseconds to minutes. Placing all signals on one time grid can distort the directed relationships estimated from them. Unmeasured common influences can also make one signal appear to drive another. We introduce rate-matched Granger causality (RMGC), which estimates directed predictive relationships without a common sampling grid. Each relationship receives a robustness value, the strength of the weakest common influence found within a specified class that can reproduce it. A neural extension tests for nonlinear relationships. In a controlled benchmark, RMGC recovered more true relationships than four established methods and an autoregressive model on a common grid (92% at a false-positive rate of 5%). Given the same signal features, the common-grid model matched this recovery but had more than twice the false-positive rate, and it reversed the relationship from respiration to heart rate. The robustness value never overstated the strength of the driver behind a spurious relationship, even for drivers outside the searched class. It separated true from spurious relationships better than predictive strength did. In overnight sleep recordings and two awake datasets, many brain–heart relationships could be reproduced by common drivers no stronger than measured respiration. Robustness values only partly identified those that appeared when respiration was omitted, particularly during wakefulness. Surrogate analyses showed elevated background rates in one awake dataset. The approach applies to other signals recorded at different rates or as events, provided that influences act with a delay.

entries.title: Adaptive Beamforming Using One-Bit Data Samples for Covariance Estimation
entries.abstract: The use of one-bit quantized complex-valued data samples enables efficient distributed computation of an array data covariance. This reduced complexity covariance estimate can be used for adaptive beamforming, but requires careful diagonal loading and results in lower performance compared to a full-precision approach. Two main approaches are presented: a covariance matrix built out of complex one-bit data samples, and a “hybrid” cross-covariance between the one-bit data and the full precision data. Signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) estimates for the associated population and finite-sample matrices are derived and compared to the full precision results using tools from linear algebra and statistics. Many strong, well-separated interferers with low overlap with the signal of interest are assumed throughout, none of them dominant.

entries.title: Black-Box Comparator-Adaptive Network Regret
entries.abstract: We study comparator-adaptive decentralized online learning with network regret, which evaluates each node's prediction on the loss of every node in the network. We show that existing gossip-based algorithms are fundamentally limited for this task, and cannot achieve sublinear network regret with only one gossip step per decision round. To prove this, we construct a two-node counterexample, which shows that gossip-based algorithms can produce exponential regret despite bounded disagreement, resolving a previously open question in the literature. We then introduce a black-box reduction, which uses local learners with sublinear comparator-adaptive regret to obtain sublinear comparator-adaptive network regret. Each node exchanges predictions with its neighbors once per decision round, and a universal choice of edge weights works on every connected undirected graph without graph preprocessing. We also characterize admissible edge weights and show how weights adapted to the graph improve the regret bound. For example, for the complete graph, this improvement is quadratic in the number of nodes. Experiments on synthetic and real-world data illustrate the counterexamples we propose and compare the reduction with decentralized baselines.

entries.title: A Proposal for Multiplierless RLS Adaptive Filters with Implementation Complexity Constraint
entries.abstract: The so-called sum-of-powers-of-two arithmetic has the advantage of using simple shift and thus avoiding multiplications operations. In this work, we provide a feasible RLS adaptive filter algorithm employing the SOPOT representation. This reduces the computational burden of the RLS algorithm. Therefore, leading to a reduction in the power consumption from a hardware implementation point of view, which is an important feature in the developing of smaller, lighter and more power-efficient portable devices.
entries.journalRef: 2020 IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems (ISCAS), IEEE, Oct 2020, Seville, Spain. pp.1-5

entries.title: Optimal Window Design for Intercarrier and Intersymbol Interference Power Minimization in w-OFDM
entries.abstract: Block transceivers are essential for modern communication systems, and they are vastly implemented in many day-to-day devices, especially the orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) technique. The application of a pulseshaping technique in the OFDM generates the so-called windowed OFDM (w-OFDM). This letter proposes an optimization of the window shape, obtaining minimal intercarrier and intersymbol interference power, ICI, and ISI, respectively. A communication system is simulated by implementing the optimized w-OFDM, and its performance is compared with a non-optimized system using a raised-cosine window.

entries.title: Timestep Selection in Diffusion-Based OTFS Channel Estimation
entries.abstract: Diffusion-based channel estimators are run with a few deterministic sampling steps, and their step count is treated as a knob that trades accuracy against latency. We show that for the mean squared error this trade-off mainly comes from the default leading timestep spacing, whose first timestep indicates an intermediate noise level although the initial state is pure noise. In a multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal time frequency space receiver with ray-traced paths and per-path Doppler shifts, moving only the first timestep of the default spacing to the pure-noise end recovers the gain of trailing spacing, completely for our anchored residual estimator and mostly for a published diffusion estimator. With trailing spacing one to three steps give the most accurate single trajectory of our estimator at every signal-to-noise ratio we test, and longer trajectories raise the error, by 0.34 dB over one step at a signal-to-noise ratio of 20 dB after 50 steps. This is the direction predicted by an idealized analysis in which a long deterministic trajectory turns the posterior mean into a posterior sample. With three trailing steps, the published estimator reaches 0.8 to 1.8 dB lower normalized mean squared error than with its original five leading steps, on its own trained network and test set. A start rule that places the first timestep from the error power of the linear anchor of the estimator, with one threshold per network, recovers trailing spacing for our estimator and matches start timesteps tuned separately for every signal-to-noise ratio on a noise-prediction network. A regression network with the same architecture and data reaches 0.23 to 1.36 dB lower normalized mean squared error than the best diffusion configuration we evaluate. The step count of a diffusion channel estimator should therefore be judged only after its first timestep is fixed.
